title: The two determinant polynomials reduce to the coprime CRT factors
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $f\in A[X]$ monic. Let $g_0,h_0\in(A/I)[X]$ be monic and coprime with $\overline f=g_0h_0$. For $e\in B=A[X]/(f)$ assume its images in $(A/I)[X]/(g_0)$ and $(A/I)[X]/(h_0)$ are respectively 1 and 0 under coefficient reduction. In the power basis [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free] of B, let T and P be the matrices of multiplication by X and e. Then $D(T,P)$ and $D(T,1-P)$ [def-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly] reduce to $g_0$ and $h_0$, respectively. No idempotence of e before reduction or Jacobson hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, proof of (3) implies (1), splitting and characteristic-polynomial paragraphs; matrix formula and omitted details written out by G2

proof.text: Coefficient reduction identifies the scalar-extended monic quotient with (A/I)[X]/(fbar). Chinese remainders for the coprime factorization identify this quotient with the product of the quotients by g0 and h0. The residue hypotheses identify P with projection (1,0); multiplication by X is multiplication by X on both factors.

Concatenate the power bases of the two CRT factors. In this basis the matrix defining D(T,P) is block diagonal with the characteristic matrix on the g0 quotient and an identity on the h0 quotient. Its complementary matrix has the identity on the first and the characteristic matrix on the second. Their determinants are g0 and h0 because multiplication by X on a monic quotient has characteristic polynomial the defining polynomial.

Determinants commute with coefficient reduction and are invariant under conjugation by the CRT basis change, so these identities give the two stated reductions in the original basis. For a zero quotient ring all polynomial equalities hold; an empty block from a degree-zero factor has determinant one.

lean.statement: theorem adjoinRoot_idempotentCharpoly_map {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (g₀ h₀ : (A ⧸ I)[X]) (hg₀ : g₀.Monic) (hh₀ : h₀.Monic) (hcoprime : IsCoprime g₀ h₀) (hfactor : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ * h₀) (e : AdjoinRoot f) (he₁ : AdjoinRoot.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f g₀ (hfactor.symm ▸ dvd_mul_right g₀ h₀) e = 1) (he₀ : AdjoinRoot.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f h₀ (hfactor.symm ▸ dvd_mul_left h₀ g₀) e = 0) : let b := (AdjoinRoot.powerBasis' hf).basis; let T := Algebra.leftMulMatrix b (AdjoinRoot.root f); let P := Algebra.leftMulMatrix b e; (Matrix.idempotentCharpoly T P).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ ∧ (Matrix.idempotentCharpoly T (1 - P)).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = h₀
